title: The Heart by Kait Kerrigan, Anne Eisendrath, and Ian Eisendrath at Ro...
transcript: I forgot how much a musical hits when the book is strong, and this one hits all the right notes. The Heart begins with Simon Lamar getting into a car crash and falling into a coma by the time his parents arrive at the hospital. We learn a bit more about him through some flashback moments while his parents are processing what's going on. At this point, I was kind of wondering, “Okay, are we really gonna spend 90 minutes rehashing his life for the sake of showing how obviously sad it is for a 19-year-old to die?” I was completely incorrect in this assumption, and grew more and more fond of this show as it progressed and continually subverted my expectations. For one, the music is very electronic — not actual EDM, but probably the most EDM-influenced musical score I've ever heard. It's uniquely paired with emotional subject matter and it gives the show a pulsing quality that reflects the urgency of the narrative. Instead of entirely focusing in on the crash victim, the show is more like Come From Away in that there's an inciting event that provides a window into the lives of many different characters who are impacted in one way or another. It's funny, moving, and a really cool celebration of life and modern medicine. Tears may be shed, but this is not a gratuitous tear-jerker — it'll have you crying and then bumping in your seat two minutes later. I loved the devastating performances from Joaquina Kalukango and Jason Tam, and the little production details like the clock on the wall that progresses to the beat of the music. Nothing beats good material though — the book hits that sweet spot where you feel for every character and the dialogue is natural, and the score is such a vibe. I didn't love all of these actors’ voices for this style of music, but I'd never discourage the idea of new genres in musical theatre, especially when it produces scores like this.
